diagnostics.message: `:resource.aws_iam_instance_profile.instance` sets `role = local.aws_iam_role_instance_name`, a string computed from locals/vars rather than a reference to `:resource.aws_iam_role.instance`. Terraform can therefore create the instance profile before the role exists, and the IAM API fails with NoSuchEntity. The profile must be ordered after the role (both use the same `var.create_runner_iam_role` count, so a direct reference is safe).

`:resource.aws_launch_template.gitlab_runner_instance` sets `iam_instance_profile { name = local.aws_iam_role_instance_name }` — a derived name string, not a reference to `:resource.aws_iam_instance_profile.instance`. Nothing orders the profile before the ASG launches its first instance, so the instance launch can fail because the IAM instance profile does not exist yet. No clean attribute-level fix exists here (the reference is inside a nested block and the profile is conditionally created), so an explicit `depends_on = [aws_iam_instance_profile.instance]` (a no-op when the profile count is 0) is the right closure.

`:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.instance_docker_machine_policy` attaches to the runner agent role by name only (`role = local.aws_iam_role_instance_name`); it has no reference to `:resource.aws_iam_role.instance`, so Terraform may attempt the attachment before the role exists and fail. Add a dependency on the role resource.

`:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.instance_session_manager_policy` uses the derived role name (`local.aws_iam_role_instance_name`) instead of referencing `:resource.aws_iam_role.instance`, so the attachment can race ahead of role creation and fail. Add a dependency on the role resource.

`:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.instance_session_manager_aws_managed` attaches the AWS-managed SSM policy using only a derived role name string; it does not reference `:resource.aws_iam_role.instance`, so the attachment may be created before the role and fail. Add a dependency on the role resource.

`:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.user_defined_policies` attaches caller-supplied policies to the runner agent role by name string only, with no reference to `:resource.aws_iam_role.instance`. When the module creates the role, the attachment can be attempted before the role exists; add a dependency on the role resource (harmless no-op when `create_runner_iam_role` is false).
